utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. I already invite the usher to escort the witness into the courtroom, and meanwhile we'll deal with one matter, but I'm a bit surprised. I might need Mr. Lukic for that. Because yesterday Defence confirmed that the list of its remaining witnesses which I read out in private session is correct. The Chamber then asked the Defence to confirm its intention to withdraw all remaining Rule 92 ter motions related to witnesses not on that list, and the Chamber is seeking confirmation by the Defence, confirmation for the record, that these remaining motions are withdrawn or advise the Chamber in any other way. Mr. Stojanovic, could you respond?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. In the course of the day, we will inform the Chamber officially about that decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then we'll hear from you very soon. Good morning, Mr. Matijevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Matijevic, before we continue, I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony yesterday, that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Mr. Traldi will now continue his cross-examination. Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have Exhibit P3866 for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is a document from CSB Banja Luka reflecting the conclusions reached at an expanded meeting of the centre council held on the 6th of May, 1992. Now, first, what was the centre council of the CSB?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember well, at that time, I was not yet chief of the police section at the CSB because Stevan Markovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir -- sir, I'm going to interrupt you.

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- got killed only in July.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I hadn't asked about what your position was at the time. At the moment, my question is specifically what's the centre council of the CSB? Do you know? And if so, can you tell us.

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with the details about the centre council, but I know the centre council existed. In fact, I would rather call it the collegium of station chiefs of the Security Services Centre, and that centre council occasionally convened under the supervision of the centre chief because I attended a couple of its sessions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, if we scroll to the bottom of page 1 in both languages, we see reference to a number of participants in that discussion, and that continues on page 2 in the English. We see there the heads of the CSB departments and the chiefs of many of the subordinate SJBs at the time; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning to point -- to page 2 in both languages, we see conclusions proposed by Mr. Zupljanin. And looking at point 4 he says: "All my orders conveyed orally, as well as those I may forward by dispatch, must be carried out: They are your law. The chain of command, commanding and execution are clearly distinguished in this service. If any one of your staff should refuse to act upon an order, just inform him that he is fired; we have to get rid of the old idealogy and concepts not suited to the present moment." Now, this reflects Mr. Zupljanin's view of the importance of the MUP hierarchy that you described at the end of the day yesterday; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning to page 5 in both languages, at the end, we read: "The chief of the CSB Stojan Zupljanin informed the members of the centre council present at this meeting that he had established a special counter-sabotage and counter-terrorist police unit of about 150 to be deployed in these regions in the most complex security operations." Now, this is a reference to the special police detachment of the CSB that you also mentioned in your testimony yesterday; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have P7159. This is a report on the formation and activities of the CSB Banja Luka special police detachment. And we're just waiting for the English. If we could have page 2 in the middle in English and the fifth paragraph on page 1 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We read: "In April 1992, the government of the Autonomous Region of Krajina with the knowledge of all municipality executive committees from the region and with the approval of the Banja Luka Corps' military security administration, passed the decision on the formation of a special police detachment with the Banja Luka CSB." Now, so -- the JNA 5th Corps, then, signed off on creating this detachment; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know any details about its establishment. In April, more precisely on the 6th of April, I joined the Banja Luka CSB where I reported in order to be assigned, and then in the period of April/May, I was still unassigned in the Security Services Centre until I was appointed traffic police head at the CSB. So I'm not familiar with the details of the establishment of these units.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You certainly knew the CSB was establishing a unit; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew that much. I've heard about it. We all worked in the same CSB, so we knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now can we have 65 ter 07080.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As it comes up, one of the officers in the special detachment was a man named Ljuban Ecim; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say anything precise about his position in those units. All I know is that he was a member of these units. But in what position, I really can't say anything with any certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is a detachment from SNB Banja Luka in December 1993 to the executive committee of the Banja Luka Municipal Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could have page 1 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We see they're asking for a three-room flat for Ecim. They describe him as an inspector at SNB Banja Luka and, at the bottom of the page in English, as the special police detachment's deputy commander. Does that refresh your recollection as to his role?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've said that I know he was there, he was part of these units, but I don't know what his job was. I saw him mainly as a member of the National Security Service. I didn't know anything precise, nor did I have any reason to be interested in the details of his job because his job did not in any way coincide with mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, beginning in August 1992, part of your job was to co-ordinate the deployment of police units with the VRS; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the area covered by the Security Services Centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Obviously you had to know things about the police unit to do that job effectively; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You couldn't have done your job if you were unaware of basic facts like the command structure of the unit, could you?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now turning to page 2 in English and the bottom of the first page in B/C/S, we read that Mr. Ecim was commended, awarded, and decorated a number of times for his patriotism and success in battle and good performance of a number of special work tasks in the National Security Service. His success in battle, that's directly related to your responsibilities; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say that. First of all, because I have to stress again, I know Ljuban Ecim exclusively as a member of the National Security Service who was directly subordinated to the leadership of the National Security Service. And while I was chief of the police section from August onwards, he was never specifically part of the command personnel of the police units in any battlefields where we were involved because we had a special police detachment of the CSB Banja Luka commanded by Mr. Brane Pecanac. You could have seen that name yesterday in that document, as well as the entire command structure. Mr. Ljuban Ecim appeared only as a member of the National Security Service.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, a moment ago when I first asked you about this document you said -- sorry, when I first asked you about Mr. Ecim, you said that you couldn't say anything precise about his position in the special detachment. You said: "All I know is that he was a member of these units." And now you're saying that you don't remember if he was even ever a member of the detachment?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I'm sorry. No, I'm sorry. It's a misunderstanding. I didn't say he was a member of the special unit. After the special police unit was established, when I was chief of the police section, I was sure -- I am sure that he was not then part of the command personnel. There was some other special police unit before that, and I don't know what their personnel was, what the command personnel was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm going to deal with that response in a second, but first I'd tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 07080 will receive Exhibit Number P07795.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have P7163.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we clarify. In your last answer you said: "It's a misunderstanding. I didn't say that he was a member of the special unit." However, that's how it was translated to us. You said: I only know that he was a member. Is it that you misspoke or is it that you say, "I haven't said that"? Because then we'll listen to the audio and we'll find out what you said and see whether it's you who made a mistake or whether it's one of the interpreters who may have made a mistake. Did you tell us that you just knew that he was a member or did you not say that he was a member?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said, and I repeat, as far as I know, Mr. Ecim at the time when I was not chief of the police section, he was engaged in a special unit of the CSB, but I don't know in what position. When the special unit of the police was established, Mr. Pecanac was appointed commander, and at that time I also was appointed head of the police section. At that time, I am sure ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I read to you what is on the record at this moment. You're recorded as having said: "I cannot say anything precise about his position in those units. All I know is that he was a member of these units." Is that what you said, or is that not what you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that previously when I came to Banja Luka, I knew that he was a member of the National Security Service and he was engaged in special units, but I really didn't know specifically in what position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not asking you. What is recorded -- and I repeat the question to you as well. You were asked about Ljuban Ecim. The question was: "As it comes up, one of the officers in the special detachment was a man called Ljuban Ecim; right?" Your answer was: "I cannot say anything precise about his position in those units. All I know is that he was a member of these units. But in what position, I really can't say anything with any certainty." Is that what you said or is that not what you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, please, for the record, could you repeat the number of the P number that you are calling on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: 7163. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, before I show you this document, let's just get the chronology of the special units straight. First, this special police detachment that we saw Mr. Zupljanin talking about in that meeting, that was created at the end of April 1992 and then continued until August 1992 when its members were mostly given over to the VRS; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. It is perfectly right what you said. A certain special unit existed - I don't know exactly from when - but it was until August 1992. When the structure of the special units was reorganised at the level of Republika Srpska, a new command structure was appointed --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, let's go step by step. Later, the CSB created the special unit under Mr. Pecanac that you referred to earlier and that we saw participated at Jajce; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I'll distinguish carefully between which unit. But if we could turn to page 2 of this document, and here we see an order dated 31st of December, 1992, from Mr. Zupljanin sent to the police brigade command. And he says: "In order to improve the quality of execution of combat tasks in the Banja Luka CSB police brigade," he appoints -- and the first name we see is Mr. Ecim appointed as battalion commander. So Mr. Ecim continued to be an officer in CSB units during your time as chief of crime prevention; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This document you have put up speaks to something else. It's an order from the chief of the centre to the effect that Mr. Ecim, with a number of other men, should get involved in the police brigade of the CSB of Banja Luka which, from November 1992 until sometime in May 1993, was at the front line in the area of Obudovac. And in that brigade, I know that Mr. Ecim, with a number of other men, these who are here listed, carried out assignments in the field of national security. I see here that he is named commander of the 1st Battalion. I don't know about their establishment structure exactly, but I know he was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you mention a number of other men. We see here Zdravko Samardzija, Nenad Kajkut. Were those also members of the initial CSB special detachment that existed from April to August?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know that. I'm not sure. I know that they worked at the centre, but whether they were this, I -- I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You do know, again speaking of that initial detachment, that it included members of the Serb Defence forces, or SOS; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not very familiar with this because I arrived Banja Luka in late April -- or, rather, May, and I wasn't familiar with the issues of the organisation of the work of the service in the Banja Luka area, especially with regard to the newly established units of the police or the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, the SOS, you knew that was a criminal group in the Banja Luka area; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, could we insist on getting an answer to your previous question, that you're not very familiar with matters. Were -- were SOS -- members -- were --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please. The question was whether the initial detachment Mr. Traldi spoke about, whether that included member of the Serb Defence forces, the SOS, yes or no. Do you know whether there were any SOS members of that detachment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I heard, the structure was very heterogeneous, but I really don't know details of this structure --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- and the individual characteristics of its members.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are telling us that you have no knowledge of SOS members being members of that detachment. Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I've said that I heard that the SOS existed and that people were organised in some sort of unit or structure that was called SOS, but I had no communication with them. I was in charge of different duties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I didn't ask whether you had communication with them. Those rumours you heard, did they include that SOS members were members of that special detachment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really cannot state that because I don't remember that it was so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But that was -- what was so? You said you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't have any specific information about their jurisdiction, to what degree they were integrated in the official police structures, and whether there was some parallel organisation or something like that. That's something that I wasn't aware of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did the rumours you spoke about, did those rumours include that members or at least SOS members were part of that detachment or were linked to that detachment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I've pointed out and I will repeat that I came to Banja Luka in early April, and during the first month, I had some private affairs to attend to. I had to organise my life. So I wasn't really integrated in the work of the Security Services Centre initially. Up until the moment when I started carrying out duties at the police station, I was not well-informed about what was going on. That was until the moment when the detachment was established and that was in April as part of the activities of the Security Services Centre. Because they wanted those units to have some organised form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I tried it four times, that you are apparently not answering my question but you, rather, answer questions you've put to yourself rather than my question. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 33642.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As it comes up, this will be a report from the Milos group on 12th of May, 1992. You knew Milos was part of SNB Banja Luka; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And it refers to terrorist attacks being carried out by the SOS, terrorist and other actions against citizens of Muslim, Croat, and Albanian nationality. When you agreed earlier that the SOS was a criminal group, this is the type of crimes you had in mind; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't openly say that it was a criminal group, but I know that there were persons in the first composition of the police detachment who later on did not pass the checks, the vettings, for being the members of the police, and they were dismissed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So do you now say you were unaware that the SOS was a criminal group?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I note that, as far as I know and to the best of my recollection, there were individuals in these structures who later did not meet the criteria to work in interior organs for security reasons, which seems to indicate that they had tendencies to --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not asking about tendencies. You were in Banja Luka in April and May 1992. You knew the SOS was committing crimes against non-Serbs; right? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't have any particular knowledge because I was in charge of completely different duties. I did not deal with crime at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you a follow-up question. You were asked by Mr. Traldi about the crimes of SOS as a criminal group which you earlier confirmed in one of your answers. So it was about crimes and SOS. In your answer --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't say that it was a criminal group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll read to you what you said in answer to one of the questions, and if you say that's not what you said, then we'll verify it on the basis of the audio. The question put to you was: "Well, the SOS, you knew that was a criminal group in the Banja Luka area; right?" Your answer was: "Yes." You didn't say that. We'll have that verified whether you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't put it that way but that I heard that in the composition of those --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness -- Witness, we'll check on the basis of the audio whether that's what you said, yes or no. Now I now come back to my question. When asked about whether this were the type of crimes committed by the SOS, which triggered a discussion on whether it was a criminal group or not, in your answer, you started talking about individuals who were removed from the special detachment. So I'm wondering why, if a question is put to you about SOS and its crimes, why in your answer you spontaneously start talking about individuals who were removed, and upon vetting, turned out to be not qualified to be members of the special detachment, if, as you told us earlier, you had no knowledge about SOS members being members of the special detachment. Because in this answer, you're establishing a link, not asked to do so, but spontaneously. So do you have any explanation as why a question in relation to crimes committed by SOS members, why in your answer you link them to individuals in the special detachment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am quite clear with regard to what I presented to you, but it seems there was a misunderstanding. When you asked me whether I was familiar with the SOS structure, I said that I didn't know anything or almost anything about this structure --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, let me stop you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- or I had just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you there. Let me stop you there. I'm not asking you to repeat what you said because we have the audio, we have the transcript. I'm asking why, when a question is put to you why -- crimes committed by SOS, why in your answer you suddenly link that issue with individual members of the special detachment, whether you have an explanation as why you established that link in relation to this question and this answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not creating a link between what you said, that is to say, the crimes of the SOS and the special detachment. I'm creating a link between members of the SOS as a whole and the special detachment which was established later on the orders of the centre chief from all those structures that appeared in Banja Luka. Later on, it was the police detachment and an official unit of the Ministry of Interior of Republika Srpska. I wanted to draw a line there, but somehow it seems there was a misunderstanding between the other two. I'm trying to be as clear and as direct and as specific as I can, and I've told you what I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 16981.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you done with 33642?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I am, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is an article from Glas, the 13th of May, 1992, and if we could scroll down to the bottom of the page and zoom in on the centre article on the bottom of the page in B/C/S, centre article at the very bottom of the page, we see a reference to a parade on the 12th of May in Banja Luka and the introduction of the newly formed special squad of the police. And that refers to the same special detachment; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I think, just to make sure the record is clear, that I understood you correctly a moment ago to say that you now do acknowledge that members of the SOS were incorporated into that special detachment; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender the last two documents. And that's 65 ter 33642 and 16981.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 33642 will receive Exhibit Number P07796. And 65 ter 16981 will receive Exhibit Number P07797.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7796 and P7797 are admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the Chamber has received evidence that the special detachment then committed crimes including in Bosanski Novi, P7102, Prijedor, P7209, and Kotor Varos, P3711, crimes that were known to the CSB. Two questions. First, were you aware that this special detachment had committed crimes against non-Serbs in those municipalities?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I am not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Second, as a police professional, that's what you'd expect from an armed unit composed, in part, of members of what had been a criminal group; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's an assumption which hypothetically I can explain by saying that if persons have a tendency to commit crime, then that can be expected. But I cannot support that with any facts in this particular situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to turn now to paragraph 7 of your statement which addresses Simo Drljaca, and you claim in your statement that he was replaced as chief of SJB Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And in that regard, I'm going to ask Ms. Stewart now to play a video, 65 ter 33601. Now CLSS has confirmed the translation so we'll only need to play it once.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Reporter: ... for almost a month now. "Ratko Adzic: Well, I wouldn't regard this here as being replaced. I believe that we've done this the Serbian way. This is simply a consequence of the state of war and, probably, if there is anything local about it, that concerns what happened in Prijedor, and I must say that the Serbs of this area have done colossal things here, this including, of course, the public security station. "Reporter: 'That is why,' stressed Adzic, 'the matter at hand here is not about being replaced because, with a job like the one Mr. Simo Drljaca did, he can only be promoted.' "Ratko Adzic: As regards Simo Drljaca, I am delighted that this has happened, he would perhaps himself want to have a bit of a rest, but I won't allow him to rest. On the contrary, I believe that a man such as this, such a member of staff, does indeed have work to do at the Ministry of Internal Affairs and should be one of my associates, and probably - albeit tacitly - I believe he has agreed to such a solution. As a proven member of the Serbian Democratic Party, and as a person, I hope that Simo will also be my associate, and will of course continue working on these tasks because we cannot back out now. Until we have a seal of approval for the Serbian state, we have no right to back out of the struggle. "Reporter: Yet another misunderstanding which has its roots in the recent removal of municipal authorities and of Prijedor has thus been eliminated, and the town's public security station will finally be able to devote itself more to the problems of both a war-time and civilian nature."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That was Ratko Adzic, he became the minister of the interior at the beginning of 1993; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And he was clear that Drljaca's appointment to his staff was not a replacement but a promotion; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the way we understood it, when a man moves from one position to another in circumstances that are not quite usual or specially announced, then it was believed to be a removal. I was not aware of the circumstances of his transfer to other duties, but I do know that there were some problems in Prijedor, so it's possible that both affected the fact that he was removed from one post to another.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender the video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 33601 will receive Exhibit Number P07798.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7798 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 33597.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is a dispatch dated 16 May 1994, and we see at the bottom that comes from Mr. Drljaca, now identified as chief of CJB Prijedor. By 1994, the term used for regional police headquarters was CJB rather than the original CSB; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The CJB and SJB are different organisations. The -- the CJB is --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir -- sir --

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there's an error here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: By 1994, the term for a regional police structure that had several municipalities under it was CJB instead of the original CSB; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, there were CSBs there, which were security service centres rather than public security services. I'm not sure when they were named differently as public security centres. It may have been after the war. I'm not sure what it stands for here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let's for a moment have 65 ter 33604.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This will be another portion of your sworn testimony in the Mejakic case in Bosnia. And we'll be looking at the bottom of page 23 in English and at page 25 in B/C/S. Now, you were asked about organisational changes in the MUP. This begins at line 22 in the English on the right. And you say: "In 1994, the new book of rules on the internal organisation of the Ministry of the Interior was passed, when the centre for security services Banja Luka because of its size. It was the largest centre for security service in the Republika Srpska, it was divided into several centres, namely: The centre for security services in Banja Luka for a number of municipalities in that region, but also the centre for security services in" - and we turn to the next page in English - "in Prijedor was established which had territorial jurisdiction over the municipality of Prijedor, Novi Grad, Kozarska Dubica, Kostajnica, Sanski Most, Kljuc, and Krupa. I believe at that time the name of this town was Krupa na Uni." So, first, do you stand by the testimony that I've just read back to you?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. One can see precisely here the difference between this document and the previous one with regard to the Security Service Centres and the public security centre, because, as far as I know, in 1994, Security Services Centres were in operation rather than public security stations. And public security stations are internal organisational structures of Security Services Centres at municipal levels.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And what you're clearly testifying here is that Prijedor didn't just have a municipal centre, it had a regional centre with several SJBs under it; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yet in 1994, it received a new organisational structure as one of the regional centres, yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we go back to 65 ter 33597.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, I don't know how much time you would need to finish this, but it is approximately time for a break. So if it would take too long, I would invite to you do it after the break. If you can finish it within, well, let's say, two to three minutes, then you're invited to continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think I'll be quite quick, Your Honour. And if my impression changes, I'll let the Court know and we'll break.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, we see at the top that Mr. Drljaca, as chief of the CJB, is sending this to all SJB in the region. That reflects that as head of the Prijedor CJB he had authority over the SJBs in the municipalities that I just listed; right? Kljuc, Kostajnica, Kozarska Dubica, Sanski Most, and the others.

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. Except that here I think there is a mistake in the acronym CJB, because it was CSB Prijedor, and this dispatch is from May 1994. I think this is simply a typo. CJB did not exist then as an organisation. There was CSB Prijedor and CSB Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Two last quick questions. First, being the chief of a regional centre, whatever you recall the acronym to be, that's clearly a promotion over being the chief of just one municipality; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, we can -- we can say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, second, we say that the minister here is identified as Mico Stanisic. By this time, May 1994, Mr. Stanisic was serving again as minister of the interior; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would tender the document and then I'd suggest we take the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 33597 will receive Exhibit Number P07799. And 65 ter 33604 will receive Exhibit Number P07780.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think you tendered only this document, Mr. Traldi. Is that...

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I had only tendered 33597. The witness affirmed the testimony that I'd read back to him, so I'd understood it not to be necessary to tender that portion of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So then we leave it to 33597.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 33597 will receive Exhibit Number P07799.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that is hereby admitted into evidence. We take a break. Mr. Matijevic, we'd like to see you back in 20 minutes. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with your leave, let me just say that together we have in the courtroom with us our young assistant, Rebecca Monroe, who will be in the courtroom as we continue to examine this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Welcome in the courtroom, Ms. Monroe. As a matter of fact, Mr. Stojanovic, however I'm pleased with your message, I was expecting, as a matter of fact, an answer to the question we raised earlier today, that it's about withdrawal of any remaining evidentiary motions, but then we'll hear from you later today, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we haven't forgotten. We are simply waiting to hear from Mr. Lukic who had some obligations that couldn't be postponed regarding the transfer of witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll hear later today from you. Mr. Traldi, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 33602.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, as it comes up, sir, one of the pieces of information that Mr. Drljaca relayed in the last document was your appointment as deputy chief of crime prevention for the RS MUP. That was a promotion for you, right, when you attained that position?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, yes. If I may just add, Mr. Drljaca was basically just forwarding a dispatch from the Ministry of the Interior signed by the minister. He was only informing his units on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: He was informing the SJBs underneath him; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is 65 ter 33602. This is a collection of extracts from Mr. Drljaca's MUP personnel files.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have page 40 in the English and 27 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, here we see Drljaca is temporarily assigned to duties of head of the MUP, information office as of 1 April 1993, signed by then-Minister Adzic. Now, this is his promotion to serve as one of Adzic's advisors that Adzic was talking about in the video we saw; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have page 31 in the English; 22 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This is dated 17 January 1994. We see the minister signing it is Mico Stanisic. And it's a decision -- Simo Drljaca is hereby temporarily assigned to duties and tasks of assistant chief of the Banja Luka security service centre as of 17 January 1994. Now, that's a higher position than a local SJB chief; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could say that, although the responsibilities of assistant go only as far, whereas all the powers lie with heads of centre, chiefs of centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have page 23 in the English; 17 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this document is dated 27 April 1994. We see at the bottom in B/C/S that it's signed by Minister Stanisic again. And by this decision, Drljaca is provisionally appointed to the tasks and duties of the chief of the Prijedor public security centre from 27 April 1994. Now, that's the promotion that we saw reflected in the last document before the break; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, possibly. Chief of centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning to page 16 in English, 13 in B/C/S, we see a decision dated 20 October 1995 on early promotion to higher rank. If we scroll down in the English, we see that Drljaca assigned to the tasks and duties of the chief of the Prijedor public security centre with the rank of major is receiving an early promotion to the rank of colonel. If we turn to the next page in English only, we see that it's signed by then-Minister Tomislav Kovac. And so we see again that Drljaca is being promoted; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So just to make sure we're clear, what we've now seen is three separate ministers of the interior - Adzic in 1993, Stanisic in 1994, Kovac in 1995 - all promoting, not replacing, Mr. Drljaca; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you can see that from here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And all of these promotions were well after the crimes that Mr. Drljaca's police committed in Prijedor, including at Koricanske Stijene, at Omarska camp, were well known, not just in the Republika Srpska but internationally; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Concerning these events which were later established to be crimes, at that time some of them were known; others were not. I cannot say anything about the information available and the responsibility of any chief of centre, including Mr. Drljaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, you knew at the time, surely, during the war, that the crime at Koricanske Stijene, for instance, the mass murder of Muslims there, was committed by members of the Prijedor police; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was informed although not of the details because it was the crime investigation department that conducted the investigation, the section from the public security centre Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you refer to an investigation. No one was punished in RS courts for that crime during the war, were they?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 33602 will receive Exhibit Number P07800.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have P6952.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As it comes up, you say in paragraph 8 of your statement, that Drljaca was close to the Prijedor Crisis Staff. Now, you know he was a member of the Prijedor Crisis Staff; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, by virtue of his position. And pursuant to the order on the establishment of Crisis Staffs, a chief of the public security centre would automatically become member of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And similarly, for instance, Mr. Zupljanin was part of the regional Crisis Staff for the Autonomous Region of Krajina, the ARK; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know he was a member.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, in 1992, Mr. Drljaca's reports, they were supposed to go to Mr. Zupljanin at the CSB; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, by the line of reporting.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And so what we see here is 30 April 1992, that's the date of the take-over of Prijedor; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't remember if that's the date, but if it's written here, it's possible. I don't know the exact date of the take-over of power.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you'd agree that what is reflected here is Drljaca reporting up to the CSB immediately the day of the take-over; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's noted here, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 16024.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This is a document coming from Mr. Drljaca, then the head of SJB Prijedor, on 11 May 1992. We see a reference to a meeting of the council of the Security Services Centre in Banja Luka on 6 May 1992, the meeting we saw earlier, and a number of conclusions. Turning to the end in both languages of this document, we see Drljaca requires his station commanders to brief their employees on the conclusions from this meeting. Now, that's an example of Drljaca relaying Zupljanin's direction, the CSB's direction, down his own chain of command in Prijedor; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what we see from this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd tender the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 16024 will receive Exhibit Number P07801.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7801 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 02578. This is a CSB Banja Luka decision dated the 28th of April [sic], 1992, type signed by Mr. Zupljanin. Number ending 09399, informing subordinate SJBs that employees who did not sign solemn declarations are dismissed as of 15 April 1992. I think I may have misspoken. It's dated the 28th of May, and I said - or at least am recorded to have said - the 28th of April. But it refers to this decision, 28 May, that employees who didn't sign solemn declarations are dismissed. Now if we could have 65 ter 16946.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is a list of Prijedor SM employees who signed the solemn declaration and of those who did not dated the 29th of May, 1992, the next day. Now, would you agree with me that we see here the information necessary to implement the CSB decision we just saw has been collected by the Prijedor SJB the day after the decision was issued?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It follows from this document except that it says "SM Prijedor," which means the station of police. It doesn't reflect the whole personnel of the public security station. There may be more.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the way that the direction about people who signed the solemn declaration and those who did not would have gotten from the CSB to the police station is it would have been relayed down the chain by the SJB to the SM; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Because the police station, "stanica milicije," is part of the public security station.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 16951.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And here we see a document sent by Drljaca also on the 29th of May --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, 16951. We still have 591 --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Here we see a document send by Mr. Drljaca also on the 29th of May to the Banja Luka CSB in response to a different communication dated the 28th of May, 1992, and reporting here on the structure of the Prijedor police. So, again, we see next-day response and implementation of the order, the direction coming down from the CSB; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you can see that from this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can we go to the bottom of the English. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would tender 65 ter 02578, 16946, and 16951.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 02578 will receive Exhibit Number P07802. 65 ter 16946 will receive Exhibit Number P07803. And 65 ter 16951 will receive Exhibit Number P07804.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7802, P7803, and P7804 are admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have P3434, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is a weekly report from CSB Banja Luka for the period of the 18th [sic] to the 25th of May, 1992. These weekly reports were send to the RS MUP headquarters; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Whether they were forwarded in the original or not, I don't know, but, yes, it went through the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have page 2, paragraph 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, we see a reference to fighting the escalation of the situation in the Prijedor area. Then we see a reference to an order by the Prijedor Military Command and the army carrying out an artillery attack on Hambarine, and then a vigorous mopping-up operation in Kozarac. This is information that would have come up to the CSB from SJB Prijedor; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, logical.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And this one of the operations where based on the standard practice that you described earlier yesterday, police units participating would have been resubordinated to the VRS command; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 02689. This is an RS MUP daily bulletin describing events on the 26th of May, 1992. If we turn to page 2, in the -- sorry, page 2 in the English only. Still page 1 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Under Banja Luka CSB, we see a reference to, on the 26th of May, armed clashes involving the Serbian army and what are described as Muslim extremists in the municipality of Prijedor, particularly around the village of Kozarac. And if we scroll now to page 2 in the B/C/S and the bottom of this page in English, we see the recipients, the minister of the interior, under-secretaries, office of the minister, and the RS government. So through these daily bulletins, information would flow from Prijedor all the way up to the prime minister, Mr. Djeric; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. That's how this was circulated.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 02689 will receive Exhibit Number P07805.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And could we have 65 ter 19184.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: These are Minister Stanisic's instructions for providing details for the daily bulletin to all CSBs dated 18th of April, 1992, ordering the CSBs to send the daily incident bulletin and other significant information of security interest to the ministry by fax. All CSBs were responsible for keeping the ministry informed in this way; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And that was to ensure that the flow of information that we just saw worked properly and allowed the RS leadership to know what was going on on the ground; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 19184 will receive Exhibit Number P07806.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7806 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have P2895.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: One of the places that I'd earlier asked you if you knew --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: One of the places that I earlier asked you if you were aware that Prijedor police committed crimes against non-Serbs was Omarska camp. Now, this is Mr. Drljaca's order establishing the camp. You've seen it in your testimony in the Mejakic case; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was an expert witness in the Mejakic case based on the available documents from the Court of Bosnia-Herzegovina. And I was not aware of this because it comes from May 1992 when I did not hold any position in this area and Security Services Centre, but I was, rather, in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you were certainly aware at some point in 1992 that the Prijedor police was committing crimes against -- members of the Prijedor police were committing crimes against detainees at Omarska; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that there were many security problems in the Prijedor area, but I did not visit the area at the time. It was not even possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir -- sir, I'm not asking you about your travel then. I'm asking specifically: Were you aware at some point in 1992 that members of the Prijedor police were committing crimes against Omarska detainees?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Up until the Koricanske Stijene incident, I didn't know anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the Chamber has received evidence - P7209 - that the CSB knew that members of the special detachment had committed crimes against Omarska detainees by early June 1992. Did you also miss this information?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with that because I was in charge of other duties at the time at the public security station in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, if we turn to page 3 in the English and the end of the document in B/C/S. In B/C/S, we still have a different document, I'm afraid. I'm looking for point 17 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And we see the implementation of the order to set up the camp shall be supervised by police chief Dusan Jankovic in collaboration with the Banja Luka CSB and with the support of authorised executive personnel. Now, the CSB level, the regional police was directly involved in setting up Omarska; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware of that at the time. With regard to Omarska, I only learned about it in my role as expert witness in the Mejakic case.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In your statement, paragraph 8, you say you recall that Mr. Drljaca usually made decisions without consulting with the Banja Luka CSB. Now, when I show you an order from him, you tell me you didn't know about the decision he was making. In fact, you weren't familiar with or privy to the decisions Drljaca was making on the ground or his reporting to or consultations with CSB Banja Luka during the summer of 1992, were you?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I took over the duty of the chief of police, then I was informed. But up until then, including this document, it was not objectively possible for me to know this because I worked at the public security station in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 32036.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I seek confirmation of one of the previous answers. You told us that as an expert in the Mejakic case, it was then that you learned about Omarska. You never heard or learned about crimes having been committed in Omarska before that Mejakic case which, if I understand well, you gave your testimony in 2008. You never heard about Omarska crimes before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not in any specific way and not about any details. I knew what any citizen knew. But I left the service in 1995 and I was not really present in the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did every citizen know that crimes were committed at Omarska?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I cannot put it that way. But it was known that there were crimes and certain problems, but being specific is something else. And I didn't really deal with that. I never even went there physically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You say "it was known that there were crimes and certain problems." It was known that prisoners there, detainees there, were being killed; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you could put it that there were some indications, but I cannot really confirm anything specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It was known at the CSB level, it was known widely throughout the ARK, that people being held there had been murdered; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot comment on or convey impressions or information that citizens had at the time. But as we had a situation of war in the general area, people perished everywhere. It was known that there were victims in the Prijedor area, certainly so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, from August 1992 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you one thing. You say: I cannot comment on what other citizens knew. You told us that you knew what all the citizens knew. So therefore apparently you are aware, otherwise you couldn't say: I knew what everyone knew.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I have stated my mind well, I didn't know anything about specific events. But one could hear that there were many security problems in the Prijedor area, on both sides.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But, again, the focus of the question was whether you knew about detainees being killed, not only as a citizen but also whether this was widely known within the -- within your police circles. Apart from details - who exactly, when exactly - but was it known that detainees were killed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was not aware of that, really.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'd ask that the witness be given Rule 90(E) advice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I missed that. Witness, the Prosecution asked me to inform you about a rule in our Rules of Procedure and Evidence, and I read it to you. Let me see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The rule reads: "A witness may object to making any statement which might tend to incriminate the witness. The Chamber may, however, compel the witness to answer the question. Testimony compelled in this way shall not be used as evidence in a subsequent prosecution against the witness for any offence other than false testimony." Which means if a truthful answer to a question might tend to incriminate yourself, then you can ask to be relieved from the duty to answer that question. But if you answer the question, it should be fully in accordance with the truth. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have page 47 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, this is a recording of an OTP interview with Colonel Bogojevic who you testified yesterday that you had contact with, that you co-ordinated with, that you had a good working relationship with. Now, he is asked here beginning at line 19: "Colonel, tell me about Omarska." And he starts: "I know bad things about Omarska." And then at the end of his answer, after referring to some other camps as well, says that: "The conditions in the camps were very bad, very complex. Those camps, I could almost say for certain, were collection centre -- centres where all categories of the population were rounded up and taken regardless of age or combat fitness." Now, my question is: Did Colonel Bogojevic, during his communications with you, tell you the bad things he knew about what was going on in Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that we ever discussed those matters because I simply had no special reason to deal with Omarska, as I've said before. Because I was never involved in any way in any activities in the Omarska area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So as -- as chief of crime prevention who had what you earlier described as indications that detainees there had been murdered, you considered yourself to have no special reason to do anything about what was happening in Omarska. Is that your testimony today?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please. I was chief of the police department at the Security Services Centre in Banja Luka, not the chief of the crime prevention department. And police precisely did not investigate crimes but was in charge of some other duties, if we understand each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You were later deputy chief of crime prevention for the whole RS; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in Bijeljina. In 1994, I was transferred there. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And it is correct that in neither of those positions did you take any steps to investigate the indications that you'd received that prisoners at Omarska had been murdered; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The crime prevention administration in the Ministry of Interior was a place where I discharged duties as assigned by my superiors. I never received any duties or had any authority to deal specifically with such activities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I may just get clarity. Is your answer that in fact you didn't do such investigations, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I didn't take any measures, because I did not have any authority. I was not authorised by my superiors to discharge such duties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have P3874.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we are waiting for that, could you tell us who had the authority and who would have had to do it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The public security station that was territorially in charge, that is to say, the Prijedor Security Services Centre and public security station. First it was the Banja Luka Security Services Centre and then the Prijedor one, they were in charge of carrying out investigations in the area that they were in charge of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And do you know whether they ever did that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't know that. I know, for example, about Koricanske Stijene, that there was an investigation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now this is a document sent by Mr. Zupljanin to the RS MUP on 20th of July, 1992. Directing your attention to the second paragraph in both languages, we read: "However, during these conflicts, representatives of Army of Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and police arrested a great number of citizens of Muslim and Croat nationality who were, depending on the number and the circumstances in the field, sent to various buildings like schools, centres, factory facilities, open spaces, and so on." Now, you were aware of the detention by the VRS and the RS MUP of a great number of Muslim and Croat citizens in the ARK in the summer of 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was certain information that there were arrests and detentions and other activities in the areas of certain public security stations why -- which was why the Security Services Centre sent dispatches urging everyone to take measures as prescribed by law; that is to say, releasing persons who were unlawfully detained when there was no basis to keep them in detention.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let's see what Mr. Zupljanin says about that. He describes three categories into which detained persons were placed. And then, turning to page 2 in the English, the first two categories are described as "of security interest to us." Then --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sorry, we have to start at the bottom of page 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Where is it in B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It's on page 2 in the B/C/S as well. Thank you, Your Honour. In the top paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: He says: "The third category of these prisoners is composed of adult men about" - turning now to page 2 in the English - "about whom the service does not have any information of security interest for us so far. Therefore, they can be treated as hostages." That's very different from saying: Act in accordance with the law and release them as you just claimed, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, what is noted here is different. That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It's consistent with what we saw Colonel Bogojevic describe, the rounding up of people regardless of age or combat fitness for detention in camps; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, in fact, you were aware that people who the VRS and the RS MUP had no basis to detain were being held and in your boss's view at the time - Mr. Zupljanin's - they could be used as hostages; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm really not aware of that part because I know that the centre chief officially advocated that everyone be processed in accordance with the law. I'm really not familiar with this word "hostages."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, did you refer to Colonel Bogojevic or Blagojevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Bogojevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Finally, in this regard, sir, the Chamber has received evidence that the same categorisation, same type of three categories was used at Omarska, which we were discussing earlier. That's a reflection of CSB Banja Luka protocols, as we see Mr. Zupljanin referring to here, being used in the camps in Prijedor; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that, but if the centre chief noted it, then it must be so. But I was not involved in this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm about to turn to another topic. I see it's a minute or two early, but I'd suggest for continuity that we break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, as a matter of fact, I think we resumed at five minutes to rather than ten minutes to, but let's take the break now and then be on track again. The witness may follow the usher. We'd like to see you back in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, could you tell us where you are, approximately, in terms of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I would expect to be finished within the first half of the next session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First half of the next session. Mr. Stojanovic, could you give us already an impression about how much time you think you would need.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm missing interpretation at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At this moment, I think I will have several topics to cover, and I suppose it will take about ten minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Which would leave time later today to deal with a few procedural items, and hopefully we could conclude those today so that we don't have to schedule a hearing tomorrow just for these practical matters. We take a break and we'll resume at ten minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we're waiting for the witness, Mr. Stojanovic, you're on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, Your Honour. After consultations with my colleagues from the team, I just wish to inform you officially for the record that, as far as we are aware, we have no further motions regarding witnesses under Rule 92 ter. But if we have omitted something, overlooked something, you may consider that we have no further motions for hearing witnesses under 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The question was about 92 bis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I think it was about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: 92 bis -- 92 ter?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 92 ter. Because we discussed the witnesses still to appear in court. Yeah. That's on the record, Mr. Stojanovic. Mr. Traldi, if you are ready, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Can we have 65 ter 13129.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This is an RS presidential decree from 28 June [sic] 1995. The second name we see is promoted to the rank of major-general is Vladimir Arsic. Now, in 1992, he was commander of the 43rd Brigade in Prijedor. The MUP units that you said would have been subordinated to the VRS during combat in Prijedor, they would have been subordinated to him; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under the rules of engagement of police members in combat operations, they were resubordinated to military commands.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And so the ones in Prijedor would have been resubordinated to the command of the 43rd Brigade, Arsic; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In combat operations. Not in their regular work.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 13129 will receive Exhibit Number P07807.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have Exhibit P358. This is one of General Mladic's notebooks from the war. Could we have page 151 in the English, 155 in the original B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Here we see at the beginning of General Mladic's notes of a meeting in Banja Luka on the 27th of May, 1993. Turning to page 154 in English and 158 in the B/C/S original, at the bottom of the page, both languages, we see Mladic reports that -- Mladic records that Colonel Bogojevic had informed him that four or five days earlier Simo Drljaca had arrived, sent by the RS Ministry of Interior, and he came about the Tomasica mine. Turning to the next page in both languages, Mladic records the mine is near Prijedor, records "where earlier they had buried around 5.000 Muslim bodies," and writes: "I'm sure that the world knows about this from the released prisoners." Now, it's clear that we're talking about a very large mass grave here; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to this, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is also -- this the notebook entry that you referred to in your statement; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand. I refer to what?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In your statement, you comment on one of the entries in General Mladic's notebook. It's this entry; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, certainly. I explained in my statement, in fact, I answered the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, lower down, Mladic records that Bogojevic informs him the team includes -- well, first, that they want to get rid of it by burning, grinding or some other way, and that the team includes Drljaca. And then: "At the meeting were General Subotic, Arsic, Drljaca, me, and Mile Matijevic." Now, we agree Mile Matijevic refers to you; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the name we see here refers to me because in the SUP of Banja Luka there was no other Mile Matijevic. That's as far as the name is concerned. Facts are something different.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, covering up a large mass grave, covering up the evidence of that, that's not something anyone would falsely claim they themselves were involved in; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question very well. Is not something ... what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Covering up a large mass grave, that's a serious, ominous criminal activity; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We see Colonel Bogojevic says he's involved in it. Now, because this is a serious, ominous criminal activity, he wouldn't tell General Mladic he himself was involved if that wasn't true, would he?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree with the first part of what you said. Covering up such serious matters is certainly a very grave thing. As for what Colonel Bogojevic says about his involvement and the involvement of others, I will talk about that later.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: What I'm putting to you right now is people don't tend to say that they're involved in serious, ominous criminal matters to their commanding officers unless they really are. You agree with that; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you are saying is logical.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So I want to make sure I understand your evidence about this notebook entry right. As I understand your evidence, it is: First, you agree there are parts of the report that Colonel Bogojevic is giving that logically must be true; second, that it is a coincidence that you, like Colonel Arsic and Mr. Drljaca, were promoted after the cover-up of this mass grave; and, third, that Colonel Bogojevic, who you had regular contact with and a good working relationship with, is mistakenly implicating you in the serious, ominous criminal cover-up of this mass grave in Prijedor. Have I understood your evidence correctly?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, you understood it as you understood it. However, I don't agree with your statement at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I put to you that that evidence is simply not capable of belief. Do you have any comment on that?

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. I do. I will tell you very openly and very clearly and -- although it's not appropriate to make any oaths here, but I want to tell you and before this Trial Chamber concerning this specific meeting and my alleged involvement according to this document is absolutely untrue. In connection with this, I know nothing. To be quite honest, over the past few days, I was rather upset by what you said about me being promoted on account of these things. But let me accept your assumptions. May I go on? I have something more to say on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Go on, sir.

utterances.speaker: MILE MATIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said very loud and clear what my relationship and my contacts with Colonel Bogojevic were within the framework of regular assignments and regular work. Concerning these specific allegations and some issues that were touched upon in the hierarchy regarding other operations, by virtue of my position and rank, I was not able to be involved. However, when I learned of this document - I believe it was in 2010 - I was really astounded and surprised, but I was not concerned. I did not feel concerned because my conscience is absolutely clear as far as these allegations are concerned. I simply have no knowledge and no involvement in this. Let me tell you one more thing. I later kept thinking what to do about these allegations. Should I try to find out the reasons and the way my name found into this document.
